text:
DeployBot: [automated] publish finished for repo=redwood/runtime image=runtime-service:20260321-abc123 platforms=[linux/amd64, linux/arm64]
DeployBot: provenance check: MISSING attestation for platform linux/arm64 -> quarantined (publish partial). action_required
sarah.j: saw this on release dashboard — canary traffic is currently only on amd64, arm64 hasn't been promoted yet. is pull failing or is this meta-only?
miguel: it's meta-only so far; clients that prefer arm64 will get the manifest list but without attestation. still bad for compliance.
ajay: quick check: manifest list present, but arm64 image lacks cosign attestation. `skopeo inspect` shows manifest present but attestation field empty.
emily: our change window is 30m. options: 1) manual republish with attestation (~10-20m) 2) pin canary to amd64-only and delay arm64 3) rollback to previous fully-attested digest.
sarah.j: preference for republish if it's quick. who can run it?
miguel: I can try republishing from CI artifacts. steps I'll run:
```bash
# on build host
./publish_images.sh --build-id=abc123 --platform linux/arm64 --sign-attestation 
# verify after push
aws ecr batch-get-image --repository-name redwood/runtime --image-ids imageTag=runtime-service:20260321-abc123 --query 'images[0].imageManifest'
cosign verify --key ksm://projects/redwood/keys/attest-key runtime-service:20260321-abc123
```
miguel: note: if cosign uses KMS we might hit a policy/rate-limit needing ops help.
ops-bot: KMS quota snapshot: keys/attest-key - rate limit 4/s, current usage 2/s. TTL for rotated keys 12h.
ajay: fallback if republish fails: pin the canary tag to previous digest (runtime-service:20260320-prevdigest), update release notes, and hold arm64 rollout. that's safest for customer-facing stability.
emily: also need to update release notes if we do manual republish: call out that arm64 attestation was re-applied, no code changes.
sarah.j: assign: miguel -> try manual republish; ajay -> prepare rollback/pin and release-note text; emily -> coordinate release board and docs. status updates here please.
miguel: starting republish now, pulling artifacts and signing. will post verification output.
DeployBot: helper reminder: after manual republish, run `deploybot promote-manual` to register promotion and avoid duplicate canary promotions.
miguel: cosign signing step hit permission error initially: KMS policy blocked passive signing from ephemeral CI principal. escalating to ops.
ops-bot: raising ticket with KMS team, short-lived fix: add IAM pass-through for CI-runner principal for key:attest-key (will take ~7-10m).
miguel: paused until ops patch applied.
ajay: while we wait, I'm assembling the rollback playbook: commands to pin tag and update traffic routing, plus a short blame-free note for release notes. snippet:
```bash
# pin tag to previous digest
aws ecr put-image --repository-name redwood/runtime --image-tag runtime-service:canary --image-manifest '<prev-manifest-json>'
# update release notes draft
"ARM64 rollout delayed due to missing provenance attestation; rolling back canary to previous attested digest."
```
emily: good. leaving draft in /releases/notes/drafts and flagging retention for compliance.
ops-bot: KMS IAM change applied (temporary). miguel can retry cosign.
miguel: retrying cosign sign... verification now passes:
```
cosign verify --key ksm://projects/redwood/keys/attest-key runtime-service:20260321-abc123
Verification for runtime-service:20260321-abc123 -- OK
```
miguel: pushed updated manifest list with attestation for linux/arm64, ECR now shows the attestation blob present.
DeployBot: publish completed: all platforms attested. canary promotion unlocked.
ajay: promoting canary to arm64 pools across zones; watching latency, error rate for 5m.
emily: I updated the release notes: "ARM64 image was re-published to include provenance attestation; no functional changes. Monitoring ongoing." added follow-up issue to check CI KMS principal for long-term fix.
sarah.j: great work. assign postmortem if any user-facing alerts show up. otherwise we'll close this and note the KMS IAM gap in infra backlog. :thumbsup:
miguel: closing loop — manual republish + sign completed, no regressions observed after 10m.
DeployBot: thread closed by operations after successful publish.
